record.context_brief: Higher graph powers list coloring and painting
record.original_question: Fix integers k > 3 and Delta > 3. For all but finitely many connected graphs G of maximum degree Delta, is the list-chromatic number of the k-th power bounded by chi_l(G^k) <= sum_{i=1}^k Delta (Delta - 1)^(i-1) + 1 - k, and does the same bound also hold for the painting number chi_p(G^k)?

evidence.quote: Bonamy and Bousquet [16] showed, for each k > 3 and graph G with maximum degree ∆, that χ_k_ℓ(G) 6 Dk,∆ − 1. And they conjectured something even stronger: For each integer k > 3, except for a finite number of graphs G, every connected graph G satisfies χ_k_ℓ(G) 6 Dk,∆ + 1 − k.
The reasoning above suggests that perhaps also χ_k_p(G) 6 Dk,∆ +1−k, but we are unaware of any progress in this direction.

Fix integers k > 3 and ∆ > 3. For all but finitely many connected graphs G with maximum degree ∆, we have χ_k_ℓ(G) 6 sum_{i=1}^k ∆(∆ − 1)i−1 + 1 − k. The same bound holds for χ_k_p(G). This would be a list coloring, or painting, analogue of Theorem 43. (In fact, both assertions were only posed as questions.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. For an integer $k\ge 1$, the $k$-th power $G^k$ is the graph on vertex set $V$ in which two distinct vertices are adjacent iff their distance in $G$ is at most $k$. Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$.

The list-chromatic number $\chi_\ell(H)$ of a graph $H$ is the least integer $t$ such that, for every assignment of lists $L(v)$ with $|L(v)|=t$ to the vertices of $H$, there is a proper coloring $c$ with $c(v)\in L(v)$ for all $v$.

The painting number (online list-chromatic number) $\chi_p(H)$ is defined via the following two-player game on $H$ with parameter $t$. Each vertex $v$ starts with a token count $t$. In each round, Lister presents a non-empty set $S\subseteq V(H)$; Painter chooses an independent subset $I\subseteq S$ and colors the vertices of $I$ (the chosen color is the round number). After Painter's move, every vertex in $S\setminus I$ loses one token. Painter loses if some vertex has $0$ tokens and is not yet colored; Painter wins if every vertex is eventually colored. Then $\chi_p(H)$ is the least $t$ for which Painter has a winning strategy.

For integers $k,\Delta\ge 1$, define
$$D_{k,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\Delta(\Delta-1)^{i-1}.$$

Question. Fix integers $k\ge 3$ and $\Delta\ge 3$. Is it true that for all but finitely many connected graphs $G$ with $\Delta(G)\le \Delta$,
$$\chi_\ell(G^k)\le D_{k,\Delta}+1-k,$$
and does the same bound also hold with $\chi_\ell$ replaced by the painting number $\chi_p$?
artifact.status_search_result: Bonamy and Bousquet established a Brooks-type bound $\chi_\ell(G^k)\le D_{k,\Delta}-1$ for $k\ge 3$, $\Delta\ge 3$, even in the online list-coloring (painting) setting. The stronger conjecture that all but finitely many connected graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ satisfy $\chi_\ell(G^k)\le D_{k,\Delta}+1-k$ remains a conjecture by Bonamy and Bousquet; no resolution was found in the search. The analogous statement for the painting number appears to be even less studied. Status is therefore open.

status_evidence.title: Brooks' theorem on powers of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Bonamy and Bousquet proved that for k≥3, the Brooks-type bound on the chromatic number of k-th powers of graphs of maximum degree Δ≥3 can be lowered by 1, even for online list coloring.
status_evidence.claim: The known result $\chi_\ell(G^k)\le D_{k,\Delta}-1$ is established, but the stronger $+1-k$ bound is conjectural and unresolved.
